claim: When B cells encounter antigens on the surface of an antigen-presenting cell (APC), B cell receptors (BCRs) are gathered into microclusters that recruit signaling enzymes.
source: When B cells encounter antigens on the surface of an antigen-presenting cell (APC), B cell receptors (BCRs) are gathered into microclusters that recruit signaling enzymes.
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the field, supported by citations throughout the manuscript and demonstrated by the experimental data showing BCR microcluster formation.

claim: BCR microclusters move centripetally and coalesce into the central supramolecular activation cluster of an immune synapse.
source: These microclusters then move centripetally and coalesce into the central supramolecular activation cluster of an immune synapse.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1B and Video 1, showing BCR-Ag microclusters moving toward the center and forming a cSMAC within ~10 min.

claim: The coalescence of BCR microclusters depends on the actin-related protein 2/3 (Arp2/3) complex.
source: We show that this coalescence of BCR microclusters depends on the actin-related protein 2/3 (Arp2/3) complex, which nucleates branched actin networks.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing that Arp3 siRNA depletion or CK-666 inhibition of the Arp2/3 complex prevents BCR microcluster coalescence (Figure 2).

claim: The Arp2/3 complex nucleates branched actin networks.
source: We show that this coalescence of BCR microclusters depends on the actin-related protein 2/3 (Arp2/3) complex, which nucleates branched actin networks.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of the Arp2/3 complex, supported by the citation (Goley and Welch, 2006) in the Introduction.

claim: Dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling reactions in murine B cells.
source: Moreover, in murine B cells, this dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling reactions and enhances the ability of membrane-associated antigens to induce transcriptional responses and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing reduced CD79 and Syk phosphorylation when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited (Figure 6).

claim: Dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters enhances the ability of membrane-associated antigens to induce transcriptional responses in murine B cells.
source: Moreover, in murine B cells, this dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling reactions and enhances the ability of membrane-associated antigens to induce transcriptional responses and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by reduced Nur77-GFP expression in CK-666-treated B cells exposed to APCs (Figure 9B).

claim: Dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters enhances the ability of membrane-associated antigens to induce proliferation in murine B cells.
source: Moreover, in murine B cells, this dynamic spatial reorganization of BCR microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling reactions and enhances the ability of membrane-associated antigens to induce transcriptional responses and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by reduced B cell proliferation when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited (Figure 9H).

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity is important for B cell responses to spatially restricted membrane-bound antigens.
source: Our finding that Arp2/3 complex activity is important for B cell responses to spatially restricted membrane-bound antigens, but not for soluble antigens, highlights a critical role for Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin remodeling in B cell responses to APC-bound antigens.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing that CK-666 treatment reduces responses to APC-bound antigens but not to soluble anti-Ig antibodies (Figures 6C,D, 8, 9).

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity is not important for B cell responses to soluble antigens.
source: Our finding that Arp2/3 complex activity is important for B cell responses to spatially restricted membrane-bound antigens, but not for soluble antigens, highlights a critical role for Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin remodeling in B cell responses to APC-bound antigens.
evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing that CK-666 treatment does not impair CD79 phosphorylation or CD19 phosphorylation in response to soluble anti-Ig antibodies (Figures 6D, 8—figure supplement 1B).

claim: The formation of an immune synapse between a lymphocyte and an antigen-presenting cell is an excellent model for studying dynamic changes in receptor and cytoskeleton organization during cell-cell interactions.
source: The formation of an immune synapse between a lymphocyte and an antigen-presenting cell (APC) is an excellent model for studying the dynamic changes in receptor and cytoskeleton organization that occur during cell-cell interactions and how they impact cellular activation (Dustin and Groves, 2012; Harwood and Batista, 2010; Harwood and Batista, 2011; Song et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work in the field.

claim: B lymphocytes produce antibodies and cytokines.
source: B lymphocytes play a critical role in health and disease by producing antibodies and cytokines.
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell function.

claim: APCs that capture and concentrate antigens are potent activators of B cells.
source: Although B cells can be activated by the binding of soluble antigens (Ags) to the B cell receptor (BCR), APCs that capture and concentrate Ags are potent activators of B cells (Batista and Harwood, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work (Batista and Harwood, 2009).

claim: Initial BCR signaling induces localized actin severing and transiently uncouples the cortical cytoskeleton from the plasma membrane.
source: Initial BCR signaling induces localized actin severing and transiently uncouples the cortical cytoskeleton from the plasma membrane (Freeman et al., 2011; Gupta et al., 2006; Treanor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Freeman et al., 2011; Gupta et al., 2006; Treanor et al., 2011).

claim: BCR signaling output depends on BCR-BCR interactions.
source: Because BCR signaling output depends on BCR-BCR interactions, microcluster formation amplifies BCR signaling.
evidence: This is supported by the subsequent statement about CD79 phosphorylation and Syk recruitment, which are consequences of BCR clustering.

claim: BCR clustering leads to phosphorylation of the CD79a/b (Ig-α/β) signaling subunit of the BCR.
source: BCR clustering leads to phosphorylation of the CD79a/b (Ig-α/β) signaling subunit of the BCR (Abraham et al., 2016; Dal Porto et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Abraham et al., 2016; Dal Porto et al., 2004).

claim: CD79 phosphorylation allows recruitment of the Syk tyrosine kinase to the BCR.
source: This allows recruitment of the Syk tyrosine kinase to the BCR, which nucleates the formation of a 'microsignalosome', a microcluster-based signaling complex that includes the Btk tyrosine kinase, phospholipase Cγ2 (PLCγ2), and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) (Treanor et al., 2009; Weber et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Treanor et al., 2009; Weber et al., 2008).

claim: BCR signaling stimulates actin polymerization at the periphery of the B cell-APC contact site.
source: BCR signaling stimulates actin polymerization at the periphery of the B cell-APC contact site (Fleire et al., 2006), which exerts outward force on the plasma membrane to generate membrane protrusions (Mogilner and Oster, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Fleire et al., 2006; Mogilner and Oster, 1996).

claim: BCR-mediated extraction of antigen from the APC membrane occurs at the cSMAC in naive B cells.
source: BCR-mediated extraction of Ag from the APC membrane, which allows B cells to present Ags and elicit T cell help, occurs at the cSMAC in naive B cells (Nowosad et al., 2016; Yuseff et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Nowosad et al., 2016; Yuseff et al., 2013).

claim: In T cells, centripetal actin flow is a driving force for T cell receptor (TCR) microcluster centralization and cSMAC formation.
source: In T cells, centripetal (i.e. retrograde) actin flow is a driving force for T cell receptor (TCR) microcluster centralization and cSMAC formation (Babich et al., 2012; Hammer and Burkhardt, 2013; Yi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Babich et al., 2012; Hammer and Burkhardt, 2013; Yi et al., 2012).

claim: Actin dynamics are required for cSMAC formation in B cells.
source: Actin dynamics are required for cSMAC formation in B cells (Liu et al., 2012; Treanor et al., 2011) but a role for actin retrograde flow has not been established.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work (Liu et al., 2012; Treanor et al., 2011).

claim: A role for actin retrograde flow in B cell cSMAC formation has not been established.
source: Actin dynamics are required for cSMAC formation in B cells (Liu et al., 2012; Treanor et al., 2011) but a role for actin retrograde flow has not been established.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: The Arp2/3 complex binds to existing actin filaments and nucleates new filaments that grow at a 70° angle from the mother filament.
source: Alternatively, branched actin polymerization is mediated by the 7-subunit actin-related protein (Arp) 2/3 complex, which binds to existing actin filaments and nucleates new filaments that grow at a 70° angle from the mother filament (Goley and Welch, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work (Goley and Welch, 2006).

claim: The Arp2/3 complex nucleates the branched actin networks that underlie the formation of sheet-like membrane protrusions such as lamellipodia.
source: The Arp2/3 complex nucleates the branched actin networks that underlie the formation of sheet-like membrane protrusions such as lamellipodia (Pollard and Borisy, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work (Pollard and Borisy, 2003).

claim: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome is caused by mutations in either WASp or WASp-interacting protein (WIP).
source: WAS is caused by mutations in either WASp or WASp-interacting protein (WIP) (Candotti, 2018) and is characterized by increased susceptibility to autoimmune disease, recurring infections, and predisposition to lymphomas and leukemias.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work (Candotti, 2018).

claim: A20 D1.3 B cells rapidly form BCR-Ag microclusters throughout the contact site when added to APCs expressing mHEL-HaloTag.
source: When A20 murine B-lymphoma cells expressing the HEL-specific D1.3 transgenic BCR (A20 D1.3 B cells) were added to the APCs, they rapidly formed BCR-Ag microclusters throughout the contact site.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: BCR-Ag microclusters that form at the periphery move centripetally.
source: Microclusters that formed at the periphery moved centripetally.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: A cSMAC develops within ~10 min when A20 D1.3 B cells contact APCs expressing mHEL-HaloTag.
source: Closer to the center of the contact site, microclusters coalesced with each other such that a cSMAC developed within ~10 min (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: Nearly all BCR-Ag microclusters coalesce into the cSMAC after 10 min.
source: Although some BCR-Ag microclusters formed quite far from the center of the contact site (Figure 1B [yellow arrowheads]), nearly all the microclusters coalesced into the cSMAC after 10 min (Figure 1B, Video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: B cells continually extend and retract short-lived actin-rich protrusions across the surface of the APC.
source: We found that B cells continually extended and retracted short-lived actin-rich protrusions across the surface of the APC (Figure 1C [colored arrowheads], Figure 1D, Video 2), resulting in an asymmetrical cell shape.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figure 1C, Figure 1D, and Video 2.

claim: Dynamic searching mechanism allows A20 D1.3 B cells to scan a total area of ~100 µm2 on the surface of the APC over 4 min of contact.
source: This dynamic searching mechanism allowed A20 D1.3 B cells to scan a total area of ~100 µm2 on the surface of the APC over 4 min of contact and gather Ag into microclusters (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification of the area searched shown in Figure 1D.

claim: BCR-Ag microclusters form within actin-rich regions, including newly formed protrusions.
source: BCR-Ag microclusters formed within actin-rich regions, including newly formed protrusions (Figure 1C, Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figure 1C and Video 2.

claim: BCR-Ag microclusters move toward the center of the synapse along with the surrounding actin structures.
source: These microclusters moved toward the center of the synapse along with the actin structures in which they were embedded, especially as membrane protrusions were retracted (Figure 1E, Video 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kymograph analysis in Figure 1E and the imaging in Video 2.

claim: The velocities at which peripheral F-actin structures and BCR-Ag microclusters move toward the center of the synapse are similar.
source: As determined from the kymographs in Figure 1E, the velocities at which the peripheral F-actin structures and BCR-Ag microclusters moved toward the center of the synapse were similar, suggesting that actin dynamics drive the initial centripetal movement of these microclusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kymograph analysis in Figure 1E.

claim: Actin dynamics drive the initial centripetal movement of BCR-Ag microclusters.
source: As determined from the kymographs in Figure 1E, the velocities at which the peripheral F-actin structures and BCR-Ag microclusters moved toward the center of the synapse were similar, suggesting that actin dynamics drive the initial centripetal movement of these microclusters.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BCR-Ag microclusters and actin structures move at similar velocities.

claim: F-actin is cleared from the center of the contact site.
source: At the same time, F-actin was cleared from the center of the contact site and BCR microclusters within this region coalesced with each other until a cSMAC was formed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1C and Video 2.

claim: B cells exhibit largely radial spreading when they contact immobilized anti-IgG antibodies on a rigid glass coverslip.
source: In contrast to their behavior on APCs, B cells exhibited largely radial spreading when they contacted immobilized anti-IgG antibodies (an Ag surrogate) on a rigid glass coverslip (Figure 1F, Video 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1F and Video 3.

claim: B cells undergo continual outward spreading on anti-IgG-coated coverslips, reaching a contact area of ~150 µm2 after 10 min.
source: The cells underwent continual outward spreading, reaching a contact area of ~150 µm2 after 10 min (Figure 1G; see also Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 1G.

claim: B cells spreading on immobilized anti-Ig form multiple large lamellipodia, some of which persist for up to 10 min.
source: B cells spreading on immobilized anti-Ig formed multiple large lamellipodia, some of which persisted for up to 10 min (for example, Figure 1F [blue arrowheads]).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 1F and Video 3.

claim: Inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex greatly reduces the coalescence of BCR-Ag microclusters into a cSMAC.
source: We found that inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex greatly reduced the coalescence of BCR-Ag microclusters into a cSMAC (Figure 2A,B), even though there was no change in the total amount of Ag that was gathered into microclusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B) or the number of BCR-Ag microclusters that formed (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the imaging data in Figure 2A,B and Videos 4-7.

claim: Inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex does not change the total amount of antigen gathered into microclusters.
source: We found that inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex greatly reduced the coalescence of BCR-Ag microclusters into a cSMAC (Figure 2A,B), even though there was no change in the total amount of Ag that was gathered into microclusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B) or the number of BCR-Ag microclusters that formed (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B.

claim: Inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex does not change the number of BCR-Ag microclusters that form.
source: We found that inhibiting or depleting the Arp2/3 complex greatly reduced the coalescence of BCR-Ag microclusters into a cSMAC (Figure 2A,B), even though there was no change in the total amount of Ag that was gathered into microclusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B) or the number of BCR-Ag microclusters that formed (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D.

claim: ~60% of control B cells gather >90% of the Ag fluorescence into one or two large clusters at the center of the synapse by 10 min after contacting APCs.
source: By 10 min after contacting the APCs, ~60% of the B cells had gathered >90% of the Ag fluorescence into one or two large clusters at the center of the synapse, which we define as having formed a cSMAC (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Only ~15% of B cells in which the Arp2/3 complex was inhibited or depleted form a cSMAC by 10 min.
source: By contrast, many of the BCR-Ag microclusters in the Arp3 siRNA-expressing cells (Figure 2A, Video 5) and the CK-666-treated cells (Figure 2B, Video 7) did not exhibit persistent centripetal motion and only ~15% of the cells in which the Arp2/3 complex was inhibited or depleted formed a cSMAC by 10 min (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The failure to form a cSMAC when the Arp2/3 complex is depleted or inhibited is due to decreased merger of individual BCR microclusters into larger clusters.
source: The failure to form a cSMAC when the Arp2/3 complex is depleted or inhibited was due to decreased merger of individual BCR microclusters into larger clusters.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that the average size of BCR-Ag microclusters increases over time in control cells but remains unchanged in Arp3 siRNA-treated and CK-666-treated cells (Figure 2E,F).

claim: The average size of BCR-Ag microclusters increases steadily over time in control cells as the microclusters merge.
source: Consistent with this idea, the average size of BCR-Ag microclusters increased steadily over time in control cells as the microclusters merged but remained relatively unchanged over the 14 min of imaging in the Arp3 siRNA-treated cells and CK-666-treated cells (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2E,F.

claim: The average size of BCR-Ag microclusters remains relatively unchanged over 14 min of imaging in Arp3 siRNA-treated cells and CK-666-treated cells.
source: Consistent with this idea, the average size of BCR-Ag microclusters increased steadily over time in control cells as the microclusters merged but remained relatively unchanged over the 14 min of imaging in the Arp3 siRNA-treated cells and CK-666-treated cells (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 2E,F.

claim: BCR-mediated gathering of APC-bound antigens into a cSMAC at the center of the synapse is strongly dependent on the functions of the Arp2/3 complex.
source: Thus, BCR-mediated gathering of APC-bound Ags into a cSMAC at the center of the synapse is strongly dependent on the functions of the Arp2/3 complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that Arp2/3 complex inhibition or depletion prevents cSMAC formation.

claim: A20 B cells that bind to anti-IgG coated coverslips extend broad lamellipodia and exhibit radial spreading.
source: A20 B cells that bound to anti-IgG coated coverslips extended broad lamellipodia and exhibited radial spreading (control siRNA cells in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, CK-689-treated cells in Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the STED microscopy images in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A20 B cells spreading on anti-IgG coated coverslips are characterized by a dense peripheral ring of highly branched F-actin surrounding an actin-depleted central area.
source: This cell morphology was characterized by a dense peripheral ring of highly branched F-actin surrounding an actin-depleted central area that contained thin actin filaments (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the STED microscopy images in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: When Arp3 is depleted with siRNA or the Arp2/3 complex is inhibited with CK-666, BCR-induced spreading and actin reorganization are dramatically altered.
source: When we depleted Arp3 with siRNA (Figure 3A), or inhibited the Arp2/3 complex in A20 B cells using CK-666 (Figure 3B), BCR-induced spreading and actin reorganization were dramatically altered.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the STED microscopy images in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Arp3-depleted and CK-666-treated B cells extend long and loosely packed filopodia-like fibers instead of forming a highly dense, sheet-like actin network at the periphery.
source: Unlike the control A20 B cells, which formed a highly dense, sheet-like actin network at the periphery, Arp3-depleted and CK-666-treated B cells extended long and loosely packed filopodia-like fibers (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the STED microscopy images in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Aberrant actin reorganization in Arp3-depleted and CK-666-treated B cells results in substantially reduced cell spreading on anti-IgG-coated coverslips.
source: This aberrant actin reorganization resulted in substantially reduced cell spreading on anti-IgG-coated coverslips (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification of cell area in Figure 3C,D.

claim: In control CK-689-treated cells, the F-actin networks are highly dynamic at the cell edge, with actin retrograde flow rates of ~2.5 µm/min.
source: In control CK-689-treated cells, the F-actin networks were highly dynamic at the cell edge, with actin retrograde flow rates of ~2.5 µm/min (Figure 3E, Video 8).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the TIRF-SIM imaging and kymograph analysis in Figure 3E and Video 8.

claim: In B cells treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor, the peripheral actin structures are nearly static.
source: In contrast, in B cells treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor, the peripheral actin structures were nearly static (Figure 3, Video 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the TIRF-SIM imaging and kymograph analysis in Figure 3E and Video 9.

claim: Arp2/3 complex function is essential for BCR-induced actin reorganization.
source: Thus, Arp2/3 complex function is essential for BCR-induced actin reorganization and for peripheral actin dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing altered actin organization when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited or depleted.

claim: Arp2/3 complex function is essential for peripheral actin dynamics.
source: Thus, Arp2/3 complex function is essential for BCR-induced actin reorganization and for peripheral actin dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that peripheral actin structures are nearly static when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: Control B cells extend dynamic, transient actin-rich protrusions over the surface of the APC, with both lamellipodial and filopodia-like structures being observed.
source: As shown in Video 2 and Video 10, control B cells extended dynamic, transient actin-rich protrusions over the surface of the APC, with both lamellipodial and filopodia-like structures being observed (see also Figure 4A, Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Videos 2 and 10, and Figures 4A and 5A.

claim: BCR-Ag microclusters are embedded within actin-rich protrusions and move toward the cell body as these protrusions are retracted.
source: Moreover, the high spatiotemporal resolution of ISIM revealed that BCR-Ag microclusters were embedded within actin-rich protrusions and moved toward the cell body as these protrusions were retracted (Figure 4A, Figure 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 10; see also Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figures 4A, 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Video 10.

claim: B cells treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor CK-666 primarily extend long, linear, filopodia-like actin structures over the surface of the APC.
source: In contrast, B cells that were treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor CK-666 primarily extended long, linear, filopodia-like actin structures over the surface of the APC (Figure 4A, Figure 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Video 11).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figures 4A, 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Video 11.

claim: Most actin structures in CK-666-treated B cells do not retract toward the cell body over the 6.5 min observation period.
source: Most of these actin structures did not retract toward the cell body over the 6.5 min observation period.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figures 4A, 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Video 11.

claim: BCR-Ag microclusters that form on filopodia-like protrusions in CK-666-treated B cells do not translocate toward the center of the synapse or merge with other microclusters.
source: Moreover, BCR-Ag microclusters that formed on these protrusions did not translocate toward the center of the synapse or merge with other microclusters (Figure 4A, Figure 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Video 11).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figures 4A, 5A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, and Video 11.

claim: Control and CK-666-treated B cells explore roughly the same area of the APC surface over the period of observation.
source: Although the architectures of the actin protrusions generated by control and CK-666-treated cells were dramatically different, the cells explored roughly the same area of the APC surface over the period of observation (Figure 4B–E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 4B-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity is required for B cells to spread on rigid surfaces.
source: This is in contrast to the significantly reduced cell spreading on rigid anti-Ig-coated surfaces that was observed when the Arp2/3 complex was depleted or inhibited (Figure 3). Thus, Arp2/3 complex activity is requred for B cells to spread on rigid surfaces but may be dispensable for B cells to effectively probe the APC surface and form BCR-Ag microclusters under the conditions tested.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Arp2/3 complex inhibition reduces spreading on rigid surfaces (Figure 3) but not the area explored on APCs (Figure 4).

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity may be dispensable for B cells to effectively probe the APC surface and form BCR-Ag microclusters under the conditions tested.
source: Thus, Arp2/3 complex activity is requred for B cells to spread on rigid surfaces but may be dispensable for B cells to effectively probe the APC surface and form BCR-Ag microclusters under the conditions tested.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that control and CK-666-treated cells explore roughly the same area of the APC surface and form similar numbers of BCR-Ag microclusters.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-mediated actin polymerization and the resulting actin retrograde flow appear to be essential for the centralization of BCR-Ag microclusters.
source: However, Arp2/3 complex-mediated actin polymerization, and the resulting actin retrograde flow, appears to be essential for the centralization of BCR-Ag microclusters.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that BCR-Ag microclusters do not centralize when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited and actin retrograde flow is blocked.

claim: Peripheral BCR-Ag clusters in control cells move toward the center of the synapse together with, and at a similar velocity as, the surrounding actin structures.
source: Consistent with this idea, kymograph analysis showed that peripheral BCR-Ag clusters in control cells moved toward the center of the synapse together with, and at a similar velocity as, the surrounding actin structures (Figure 5B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kymograph analysis in Figure 5B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: When the Arp2/3 complex is inhibited, both BCR-Ag clusters and the associated actin structures are relatively immobile.
source: In contrast, when the Arp2/3 complex was inhibited, both the BCR-Ag clusters and the associated actin structures were relatively immobile (Figure 5B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the kymograph analysis in Figure 5B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures encage BCR-Ag microclusters, such that actin retrograde flow drives their initial centripetal movement.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures encage BCR-Ag microclusters, such that the actin retrograde flow drives their initial centripetal movement.
evidence: This is inferred from the observations that BCR-Ag microclusters are embedded in actin structures and move at similar velocities as the actin.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent initial centripetal movement of BCR-Ag microclusters appears to be required for the subsequent formation of a cSMAC.
source: This appears to be required for the subsequent formation of a cSMAC, which occurs in the actin-depleted central region of the cell.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cSMAC formation is blocked when Arp2/3 complex-dependent centripetal movement is prevented.

claim: CD79 phosphorylation occurs rapidly at the B cell-APC contact site and co-localizes with BCR-Ag clusters.
source: We found that CD79 phosphorylation occurred rapidly at the B cell-APC contact site and co-localized with BCR-Ag clusters, which were detected using an antibody that detects the surrogate Ag (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 6A.

claim: In control B cells treated with CK-689, pCD79 levels are maximal at 5 and 10 min after the B cells are added to the APCs and decline thereafter.
source: In control B cells treated with CK-689, pCD79 levels were maximal at 5 and 10 min after the B cells were added to the APCs and declined thereafter (Figure 6B), perhaps due to the internalization of BCR-Ag microclusters.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 6B.

claim: B cells treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor exhibit significantly lower pCD79 levels at the 5, 10, and 15 min time points compared to control cells.
source: Importantly, B cells treated with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor exhibited significantly lower pCD79 levels at the 5, 10, and 15 min time points compared to control cells (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: APC-induced CD79 phosphorylation increases continually over the first 30 min of B cell-APC contact as measured by immunoblotting.
source: Indeed, immunoblotting showed that APC-induced CD79 phosphorylation increased continually over the first 30 min of B cell-APC contact (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 6C.

claim: Treating B cells with CK-666 reduces APC-induced CD79 phosphorylation, especially at the 15 and 30 min time points.
source: Importantly, similar to what was observed by imaging the B cell-APC interface, treating the B cells with CK-666 reduced APC-induced CD79 phosphorylation, especially at the 15 and 30 min time points (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CK-666 treatment does not impair the ability of soluble anti-Ig antibodies to stimulate CD79 phosphorylation.
source: In contrast, CK-666 treatment did not impair the ability of soluble anti-Ig antibodies to stimulate CD79 phosphorylation (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The Arp2/3 complex-dependent spatial patterning of BCR-Ag microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling in response to polarized, membrane-bound antigens but not soluble antigens.
source: This suggests that the Arp2/3 complex-dependent spatial patterning of BCR-Ag microclusters amplifies proximal BCR signaling in response to polarized, membrane-bound Ags but not soluble Ags.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CK-666 reduces signaling in response to APC-bound antigens but not soluble antigens.

claim: B cells treated with CK-666 have significantly lower levels of pSyk at 3 min and 5 min after contacting the APCs, compared to control cells.
source: B cells treated with CK-666 had significantly lower levels of pSyk at 3 min and 5 min after contacting the APCs, compared to control cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 6F.

claim: The Arp2/3 complex is required for the amplification of the earliest BCR signaling events, phosphorylation of the CD79a/b ITAMs and phosphorylation of tyrosine residues in Syk that are required for its activation.
source: Together, these data suggest that the Arp2/3 complex is required for the amplification of the earliest BCR signaling events, phosphorylation of the CD79a/b ITAMs and phosphorylation of tyrosine residues in Syk that are required for its activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing reduced pCD79 and pSyk levels when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: CK-666-treated B cells exhibit higher levels of pCD79 prior to antigen encounter compared to control cells.
source: Although treating B cells with the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor reduced the ability of APC-bound Ags to stimulate the phosphorylation of CD79 and Syk, CK-666-treated B cells exhibited higher levels of pCD79 prior to Ag encounter (Figure 6C,D; 0 min time point).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 6C,D at the 0 min time point.

claim: CK-666 treatment increases phosphorylation of ERK and Akt in B cells prior to antigen encounter.
source: This was accompanied by increased phosphorylation of ERK and Akt, downstream targets of BCR signaling (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 7A.

claim: The median diffusion coefficients for IgM and IgD are approximately 2.8-fold higher in CK-666-treated cells than in control CK-689-treated cells.
source: Indeed, the median diffusion coefficients for IgM and IgD were approximately 2.8-fold higher in CK-666-treated cells than in control CK-689-treated cells (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the single-particle tracking data in Figure 7B-D.

claim: Both IgM and IgD have larger effective confinement diameters in CK-666-treated cells than in control CK-689-treated cells.
source: Consistent with their increased lateral mobility, both IgM and IgD had larger effective confinement diameters in CK-666-treated cells than in control CK-689-treated cells (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the single-particle tracking data in Figure 7B-D.

claim: CK-666 treatment increases both BCR mobility and tonic BCR signaling.
source: Thus, CK-666 treatment increases both BCR mobility and tonic BCR signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased BCR diffusion and increased basal pCD79, pERK, and pAkt levels in CK-666-treated cells.

claim: The Arp2/3 complex contributes to the formation of actin-based barriers that normally limit BCR diffusion and tonic BCR signaling.
source: This suggests that the Arp2/3 complex contributes to the formation of actin-based barriers that normally limit BCR diffusion and tonic BCR signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that inhibiting Arp2/3 complex increases BCR mobility and tonic BCR signaling.

claim: Treating B cells with CK-666 causes a 2.3-fold increase in the median diffusion coefficient for CD19.
source: Using SPT, we found that treating B cells with CK-666 caused a 2.3-fold increase in the median diffusion coefficient for CD19 and increased its effective confinement diameter (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the single-particle tracking data in Figure 8A.

claim: Treating B cells with CK-666 increases the effective confinement diameter of CD19.
source: Using SPT, we found that treating B cells with CK-666 caused a 2.3-fold increase in the median diffusion coefficient for CD19 and increased its effective confinement diameter (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the single-particle tracking data in Figure 8A.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures limit the lateral mobility of CD19 in the plasma membrane.
source: This suggests that Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures limit the lateral mobility of CD19 in the plasma membrane, which may be important for membrane-bound Ags to stimulate CD19 phosphorylation and augment BCR-CD19 interactions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that inhibiting Arp2/3 complex increases CD19 mobility.

claim: The initial peak of APC-induced CD19 phosphorylation is diminished and delayed in CK-666-treated B cells, compared to control CK-689-treated cells.
source: We found that the initial peak of APC-induced CD19 phosphorylation was diminished and delayed in CK-666-treated B cells, compared to the control CK-689-treated cells (Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Inhibiting the Arp2/3 complex does not impair the ability of soluble anti-Ig antibodies to stimulate rapid and robust CD19 phosphorylation.
source: As observed for phosphorylation of CD79, inhibiting the Arp2/3 complex did not impair the ability of soluble anti-Ig antibodies to stimulate rapid and robust CD19 phosphorylation (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the immunoblotting data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures provide spatial organization that is important for BCR-induced CD19 phosphorylation in response to spatially restricted membrane-bound antigens.
source: This suggests that Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin structures provide spatial organization that is important for BCR-induced CD19 phosphorylation in response to spatially restricted membrane-bound Ags.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Arp2/3 complex inhibition reduces CD19 phosphorylation in response to APC-bound antigens but not soluble antigens.

claim: In control cells, much of the pCD19 fluorescence occurs within BCR-Ag clusters at all time points after initiating B cell-APC contact.
source: In control cells, much of the pCD19 fluorescence occured within BCR-Ag clusters at all time points after initiating B cell-APC contact (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Manders' coefficient analysis in Figure 8D.

claim: The pCD19-Ag overlap is significantly less in CK-666-treated B cells than in control cells at all time points.
source: The pCD19-Ag overlap was significantly less in the CK-666-treated B cells than in the control cells at all time points.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Manders' coefficient analysis in Figure 8D.

claim: The overlap between pSyk clusters and BCR-Ag clusters in CK-666-treated cells is either not significantly different from, or is slightly higher, than in control cells over the first 15 min of B-APC interactions.
source: By contrast, the overlap between pSyk clusters and BCR-Ag clusters in CK-666-treated cells was either not significantly different from, or was slightly higher, than in control cells over the first 15 min of B-APC interactions (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Manders' coefficient analysis in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The co-localization of pCD19 with the BCR is impacted by Arp2/3 complex activity.
source: Thus, unlike pSyk, which is strongly associated with signaling BCRs, the co-localization of pCD19 with the BCR is impacted by Arp2/3 complex activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that pCD19-BCR overlap is reduced when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited, while pSyk-BCR overlap is not.

claim: The total amount of pCD19 fluorescence that overlaps with BCR-Ag clusters is much lower in CK-666-treated cells than in control cells at the 3-min time point.
source: Importantly, we found that the total amount of pCD19 fluorescence that overlapped with BCR-Ag clusters was much lower in CK-666-treated cells than in control cells at the 3-min time point.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 8E.

claim: Actin networks nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex promote APC-induced CD19 phosphorylation.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that actin networks nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex promote APC-induced CD19 phosphorylation and enhance the interaction of pCD19 with the BCR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing reduced CD19 phosphorylation and reduced pCD19-BCR overlap when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: Actin networks nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex enhance the interaction of pCD19 with the BCR.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that actin networks nucleated by the Arp2/3 complex promote APC-induced CD19 phosphorylation and enhance the interaction of pCD19 with the BCR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing reduced pCD19-BCR overlap when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate antigen induce primary B cells to undergo robust transcriptional responses.
source: In Figure 9, we show that COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate Ag induce primary B cells to undergo robust transcriptional responses, activation marker upregulation, cell size increase, and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9 showing Nur77-GFP expression, CD69 and CD86 upregulation, blast cell formation, and proliferation.

claim: COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate antigen induce primary B cells to undergo activation marker upregulation.
source: In Figure 9, we show that COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate Ag induce primary B cells to undergo robust transcriptional responses, activation marker upregulation, cell size increase, and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9C,D showing CD69 and CD86 upregulation.

claim: COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate antigen induce primary B cells to undergo cell size increase.
source: In Figure 9, we show that COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate Ag induce primary B cells to undergo robust transcriptional responses, activation marker upregulation, cell size increase, and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9G showing increased blast cell formation.

claim: COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate antigen induce primary B cells to undergo proliferation.
source: In Figure 9, we show that COS-7 APCs expressing the single chain anti-Igκ surrogate Ag induce primary B cells to undergo robust transcriptional responses, activation marker upregulation, cell size increase, and proliferation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9H showing B cell proliferation.

claim: In the presence of the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor CK-666, the APC-induced increase in GFP expression in Nur77GFP B cells is reduced to ~30% of the levels observed in control Nur77GFP B cells treated with CK-689.
source: Importantly, in the presence of the Arp2/3 inhibitor CK-666, this APC-induced increase in GFP expression was reduced to ~30% of the levels observed in control Nur77GFP B cells treated with CK-689 (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 9B.

claim: In CK-666-treated B cells, BCR-induced upregulation of CD69 and CD86 is inhibited by 40–50%.
source: In CK-666-treated B cells, BCR-induced upregulation of CD69 and CD86 was inhibited by 40–50%.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification in Figure 9C,D.

claim: CD86 upregulation in response to PMA plus ionomycin is not affected by CK-666.
source: Importantly, CD86 upregulation in response to PMA plus ionomycin was not affected by CK-666 (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9E.

claim: Inhibiting the Arp2/3 complex impairs proximal BCR signaling that is important for upregulation of CD86, as opposed to downstream events that are induced by both PMA plus ionomycin and BCR engagement.
source: This suggests that inhibiting the Arp2/3 complex impairs proximal BCR signaling that is important for upregulation of CD86, as opposed to downstream events that are induced by both PMA plus ionomycin and BCR engagement.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CK-666 inhibits CD86 upregulation in response to APCs but not in response to PMA plus ionomycin.

claim: Control and Arp3-depleted B16F1 APCs induce the upregulation of CD69 and CD86 to the same extent.
source: When primary B cells were added to these APCs, we observed that control and Arp3-depleted B16F1 APCs induced the upregulation of CD69 and CD86 to the same extent (Figure 9—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: B cells treated with CK-666 exhibit similarly impaired CD69 and CD86 responses, regardless of whether Arp3 is depleted or not in the APCs.
source: Moreover, B cells treated with CK-666 exhibited similarly impaired CD69 and CD86 responses, regardless of whether Arp3 was depleted or not in the APCs (Figure 9—figure supplement 3E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9—figure supplement 3E,F.

claim: The impaired upregulation of CD69 and CD86 observed in CK-666 treated cells is B cell-intrinsic.
source: This indicates that the impaired upregulation of CD69 and CD86 observed in CK-666 treated cells is B cell-intrinsic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that CK-666 effects on B cells are independent of Arp3 depletion in APCs.

claim: Once CK-666 is removed, B cells recover their ability to aggregate BCR microclusters and form a cSMAC.
source: Once the drug was removed, the cells recovered their ability to aggregate BCR microclusters and form a cSMAC (Figure 9—figure supplement 4B–D) and B cell activation could proceed normally, consistent with the effects of CK-666 on actin dynamics being rapidly reversible (Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9—figure supplement 4B-D and supported by a citation (Yang et al., 2012).

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes that occur during the initial stages of B cell-APC interactions are required for B cell activation responses.
source: Together, these results argue that Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes that occur during the initial stages of B cell-APC interactions are required for B cell activation responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that early but not late CK-666 addition impairs B cell activation.

claim: pnBB-treated primary B cells exhibit a slight, but not statistically significant reduction in CD69 and CD86 upregulation compared to DMSO-treated cells when added to COS-7 APCs expressing membrane-bound anti-Igκ for 18 hr.
source: When pnBB-treated cells were added to COS-7 APCs expressing membrane-bound anti-Igκ for 18 hr, they exhibited a slight, but not statistically significant reduction in CD69 and CD86 upregulation compared to DMSO-treated cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9—figure supplement 5A,B.

claim: pnBB-treated A20 D1.3 B cells are able to form cSMACs to the same extent as DMSO-treated cells when added to COS-7 APCs expressing mHEL-HaloTag.
source: Moreover, pnBB-treated A20 D1.3 B cells that were added to COS-7 APCs expressing mHEL-HaloTag were able to form cSMACs to the same extent as DMSO-treated cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 5A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data in Figure 9—figure supplement 5C-E.

claim: APC-induced activation marker expression and cSMAC formation are dependent on Arp2/3 complex activity.
source: These results suggest that APC-induced activation marker expression and cSMAC formation are dependent on Arp2/3 complex activity, whereas myosin contractility has little or no involvement, at least under these experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that Arp2/3 complex inhibition but not myosin inhibition impairs these processes.

claim: Myosin contractility has little or no involvement in APC-induced activation marker expression and cSMAC formation, at least under the experimental conditions tested.
source: These results suggest that APC-induced activation marker expression and cSMAC formation are dependent on Arp2/3 complex activity, whereas myosin contractility has little or no involvement, at least under these experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that myosin inhibition does not significantly affect these processes.

claim: Co-culturing primary B cells with anti-Igκ-expressing COS-7 APCs for 18 hr results in 30–55% of the B cells becoming larger, more granular blast cells.
source: Co-culturing primary B cells with anti-Igκ-expressing COS-7 APCs for 18 hr resulted in 30–55% of the B cells becoming larger, more granular blast cells (Figure 9G; Figure 9—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 9G and Figure 9—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: In the presence of the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor CK-666, the percent of B cells that become blast cells is reduced to 5–16%.
source: However, in the presence of the Arp2/3 complex inhibitor CK-666, the percent of B cells that became blast cells was reduced to 5–16% (Figure 9G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the flow cytometry data in Figure 9G.

claim: >90% of primary B cells that are co-cultured with anti-Igκ-expressing COS-7 APCs plus BAFF and IL-4 for 72 hr have divided.
source: CFSE dilution assays showed that >90% of primary B cells that were co-cultured with anti-Igκ-expressing COS-7 APCs plus these cytokines for 72 hr had divided (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the CFSE dilution data in Figure 9H.

claim: Addition of CK-666 to the culture reduces the percent of B cells that have divided at least once to ~55% and the mean number of cell divisions from 2 to 0.7.
source: Addition of CK-666 to the culture reduced the percent of B cells that had divided at least once to ~55% and the mean number of cell divisions was reduced from 2 to 0.7 (Figure 9H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the CFSE dilution data in Figure 9H.

claim: The reduction in B cell proliferation caused by CK-666 is accompanied by increased cell death.
source: This reduction in B cell proliferation was accompanied by increased cell death (Figure 9H), which is the alternative fate for B cells that are cultured in vitro in the absence of mitogenic stimuli.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the 7-AAD staining data in Figure 9H.

claim: When the Arp2/3 inhibitor CK-666 is added 24 hr after initiating the B cell-APC co-culture, B cell proliferation is not impaired.
source: Note that when the Arp2/3 inhibitor CK-666 was added 24 hr after initiating the B cell-APC co-culture, B cell proliferation was not impaired (Figure 9H, middle panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the CFSE dilution data in Figure 9H.

claim: CK-666 does not block cell division.
source: This indicates that CK-666 does not block cell division and suggests that the critical functions of the Arp2/3 complex in APC-dependent B cell activation occur during the first 24 hr.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that adding CK-666 after 24 hr does not impair proliferation.

claim: The critical functions of the Arp2/3 complex in APC-dependent B cell activation occur during the first 24 hr.
source: This indicates that CK-666 does not block cell division and suggests that the critical functions of the Arp2/3 complex in APC-dependent B cell activation occur during the first 24 hr.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that adding CK-666 after 24 hr does not impair proliferation.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes are important for B cells to enter S phase and proliferate.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that the Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes are important for B cells to enter S phase and proliferate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing reduced blast cell formation and proliferation when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: B cells scan the surface of the APC using complex and dynamic actin-rich protrusions that constantly extend and retract across the APC surface.
source: Using high spatiotemporal resolution imaging of actin in B cells interacting with APCs, we observed that B cells scan the surface of the APC using complex and dynamic actin-rich protrusions that constantly extend and retract across the APC surface.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the ISIM imaging data in Figures 1C, 4A, 5A and Videos 2, 10.

claim: Dynamic probing of the APC surface by B cells is mediated by Arp2/3 complex activity.
source: This dynamic probing is mediated by Arp2/3 complex activity, which also generates retrograde actin flow that facilitates the initial centripetal movement of BCR microclusters and is required for cSMAC formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing that Arp2/3 complex inhibition alters the type of protrusions formed and prevents BCR microcluster centralization.

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity generates retrograde actin flow that facilitates the initial centripetal movement of BCR microclusters.
source: This dynamic probing is mediated by Arp2/3 complex activity, which also generates retrograde actin flow that facilitates the initial centripetal movement of BCR microclusters and is required for cSMAC formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing that actin retrograde flow is blocked when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited (Figure 3E) and that BCR microclusters do not move centripetally (Figures 4, 5).

claim: Arp2/3 complex activity is required for cSMAC formation.
source: This dynamic probing is mediated by Arp2/3 complex activity, which also generates retrograde actin flow that facilitates the initial centripetal movement of BCR microclusters and is required for cSMAC formation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing that cSMAC formation is greatly reduced when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited or depleted (Figure 2).

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify proximal and distal BCR signaling in response to APC-bound antigen.
source: Importantly, these Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify proximal and distal BCR signaling, transcriptional responses, and B cell proliferation in response to APC-bound Ag.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing reduced signaling (Figure 6), transcriptional responses (Figure 9B), and proliferation (Figure 9H) when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify transcriptional responses in response to APC-bound antigen.
source: Importantly, these Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify proximal and distal BCR signaling, transcriptional responses, and B cell proliferation in response to APC-bound Ag.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing reduced Nur77-GFP expression when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited (Figure 9B).

claim: Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify B cell proliferation in response to APC-bound antigen.
source: Importantly, these Arp2/3 complex-dependent processes amplify proximal and distal BCR signaling, transcriptional responses, and B cell proliferation in response to APC-bound Ag.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the data showing reduced proliferation when Arp2/3 complex is inhibited (Figure 9H).
